Series::min_pair¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

std::pair<Series, Series> Series::min_pair(
    std::int64_t dim,
    bool keepdim = false) const

Why This Method Exists¶

min_pair() reduces each lane of one axis while preserving the provenance of the selected minimum. Its first result member is the minimum value; its second is the local int64 position along dim from which that value came.

This paired contract matters whenever the position is part of the answer. A minimum price without the period that produced it, or a minimum distance without the candidate that attained it, is often incomplete. Keeping both channels aligned also avoids independently evaluating min() and argmin().

Parameters¶

Parameter

Meaning

Default

dim

Axis reduced into one selected minimum per lane. Negative axes count from the end.

Required

keepdim

Retain dim with extent 1 in both result members.

false

There is no whole-Series overload. dim always names the axis within which positions are reported. On shape [R, C], dim=1 produces column indices for each row, while dim=0 produces row indices for each column.

Return Contract¶

The method returns std::pair<Series, Series> with synchronized members:

Member

Dtype

Shape

Meaning

.first

Source dtype

Reduced shape

Selected minimum values

.second

int64

Same as .first

Local source indices along dim

With keepdim=false, the selected axis is removed. With keepdim=true, it remains with extent 1, which is useful when the value result will be broadcast against the source. Both members stay on the source platform and own their result storage.

Selection And Gradient Rules¶

Equal minima are resolved by selecting the first position along the reduced axis. The CPU kernel writes the value and index in one lane scan; reverse mode sends incoming sensitivity only to the index stored in .second. The index channel is integer-valued and non-differentiable.

This differs deliberately from value-only min(dim): without an accompanying index, that reduction shares sensitivity across equal minima. If downstream logic must agree on one concrete source position, use min_pair() and keep the two members together.

NaN is not omitted. If the ordered reduction selects a NaN, .first contains that NaN and .second identifies its selected position. An empty reduced axis has no valid minimum and is rejected.

Examples¶

Example 1. Destructuring exposes one minimum and one local position per row.

auto values = pluss::make_series({
    {4.0, 1.0, 3.0},
    {2.0, 1.0, 6.0},
});

const auto [mins, indices] = values.min_pair(1);
std::cout << "values=" << mins << "\n";
std::cout << "indices=" << indices;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1]

Example 2. -1 selects the final axis, keepdim=true preserves it, and ties route sensitivity to the first selected position.

auto tied = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, 1.0, 5.0},
    {-4.0, -4.0, 2.0},
});
tied.tracks_slope_(true);

const auto result = tied.min_pair(-1, true);
result.first.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\n";
std::cout << "indices=" << result.second << "\n";
std::cout << "dx=" << tied.sensitivity();

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[1],
  [-4]]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[0],
  [0]]
dx=pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0, 0],
  [1, 0, 0]]

Example 3. A scalar has one value and therefore one valid local position.

const auto result = pluss::make_series(42.0).min_pair(-1);
std::cout << "value=" << result.first << "\n";
std::cout << "index=" << result.second;

Output¶

value=pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=42
index=pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0

Example 4. Reducing an empty axis fails because no lane has a candidate value.

try {
  std::cout << pluss::series::zeros({2, 0}).min_pair(1).first;
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::string message = error.what();
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

min_pair: cannot reduce an empty dimension

Undefined input, an out-of-range axis, complex ordered input, and an empty reduced axis are errors. An empty non-reduced axis is valid and yields an empty collection of lanes.
